Job Expectations

Looking for a rewarding career where your practical skills can make a real difference to our customers and communities?


Whether you've worked in telecommunications, electrical, construction, civil works, utilities, manufacturing, field services, maintenance, or a similar hands-on environment, we want to hear from you. We welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds, including apprentices, experienced professionals, and those looking to apply their transferable skills in a new industry.


At nbn, we're looking for motivated people to join our internal workforce as Customer Field Technicians. Through our fully paid 8-week training program, we'll build on your existing skills and provide you with the technical knowledge, tools and support needed to succeed in the role.


A bit about your role
As a Customer Field Technician, you'll play an important role in connecting and supporting customers in their homes or businesses across a range of nbn technologies.

Your day could involve installing new services, maintaining network infrastructure, troubleshooting faults and ensuring our customers feel supported and informed.


This is a hands-on, field-based role that offers variety and independence, with each day bringing new locations, challenges, and opportunities to learn. You'll be comfortable working both indoors and outdoors, including at heights, in confined spaces, and handling tools and equipment as part of the role.


We’ll provide full training, a company vehicle, tools of the trade, and ongoing career growth and support to help you succeed. Safety is at the heart of everything we do, and you'll be supported to follow safe work practices while delivering quality outcomes for customers and communities.

The working hours are between 7am and 7pm, with flexibility based on business needs.

A bit about you
Previous experience in telecommunications isn’t needed — we’ll teach you everything you need to know. What matters most is that you enjoy hands‑on work, like solving problems, and feel comfortable speaking with customers.

You might come from a trade, a hands‑on technical job, or a customer‑focused role. Experience in fields like plumbing, carpentry, electrical work, labouring, construction, mechanical work or manufacturing is highly valued.

You’ll do well in this role if you enjoy working independently, managing your workload, and taking pride in delivering quality work. A strong commitment to safety, clear communication skills, and a current, clean Driver’s Licence are essential.

Life at nbn
To be part of nbn is to be part of something bigger. There’s so much more from here. Our pioneering spirit drives us forward every day. Together, we help lift the digital capability of the nation by building and connecting Australia’s best fibre infrastructure into homes and businesses, plus places and things, everywhere. We’re continuing to create Australia’s network—a network made for more. Not just a way for everyone to do the things they love but transforming the way they do them.

A more inclusive working world
nbn is committed to an inclusive, flexible, and supportive workplace where everyone can feel heard, valued, and respected. We believe diverse perspectives are the key to unlocking greater outcomes and encourage applications from people of all ages, nationalities, abilities, and cultures. That's why we have a Reconciliation Action Plan, Accessibility & Inclusion Plan, offer 18 weeks of paid parental leave, are a Pride in Diversity Platinum Employer, and have active employee-led diversity pillars. Click here to see our list of employee benefits and why we're recognised as a WORK180 Endorsed Employer for Women.

About Servier

Servier in the U.S. is a Boston-based, commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company launched by Servier Group in 2018. As a privately held organization, Servier is uniquely positioned to advance cutting-edge science, tackle underserved therapeutic areas and make patients the focus of every strategic decision.

Role Summary

The Director, Thought Leader Liaison (TLL) is a strategic commercial leader responsible for overseeing the development and execution of engagement strategies with national, regional, and emerging Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) in rare neurological diseases. Reporting to the VP of Marketing, this role provides strategic oversight for the commercial relationship management of thought leaders and ensures the synthesis of actionable insights to inform brand strategy and launch planning.

The Director provides leadership and management for a national team of TLLs, focusing on team development, strategic alignment, and cross-functional integration with Marketing, Medical Affairs, Sales, and Patient Advocacy.

The Director will build and manage a team of 6 TLLs.

Team Leadership & Strategic Oversight

  • Translate corporate and brand strategy into clear operational plans for the field-based TLL team

  • Oversee the development of comprehensive KOL engagement plans across the TLL team to ensure consistency and impact
  • Guide the team in building long-term, trusted relationships with multidisciplinary care teams and centers of excellence
  • Ensure a coordinated, compliant, and customer-centric engagement strategy across the organization

Strategic Insight Synthesis

  • Synthesize field-generated insights from the TLL team to influence brand strategy, messaging, and evidence generation
  • Present high-level strategic recommendations to Commercial Leadership based on aggregated trends in diagnosis, treatment patterns, and unmet needs

Advisory Boards & Speaker Bureau Management

  • Direct the strategy for commercial advisory boards, ensuring objectives are met and insights are communicated cross-functionally
  • Provide strategic oversight for the physician speaker bureau, ensuring high-quality educational programming and compliance

Congress & Launch Excellence

  • Lead the overarching strategy for major neurology congresses, coordinating the team's engagement activities and executive leadership interactions
  • Drive launch readiness by ensuring the team identifies educational gaps and shapes peer-to-peer educational strategies at scale

Candidate Profile

Education and Required Skills

  • Demonstrated experience in people leadership, managing field-based commercial or medical teams
  • Proven success in strategic thinking and building executive-level relationship frameworks
  • Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree (MBA, PharmD, PhD, MSN, MS) preferred
  • Minimum 10+ years of pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or healthcare industry experience

  • Strong project management and organizational skills

The role. We’re hiring a Head of Engineering to build the software organization and systems that run Nox Metals. You will own technical direction, engineering execution, and team development across customer software, internal operations, data, infrastructure, and applied machine learning.

  • Work directly with sales, operations, finance, and manufacturing to understand real workflows

title: Program Coordinator I, Rural Medicine Outreach
description:
Job Title

Program Coordinator I, Rural Medicine Outreach

Agency

Texas A&M University Health Science Center

Department

Rural Medicine

Proposed Minimum Salary

Commensurate

Job Location

Bryan, Texas

Job Type

Staff

Job Description

Our Commitment

Texas A&M University is committed to enriching the learning and working environment by promoting a culture that respects all perspectives, talents & lived experiences. Embracing varying opinions and perspectives strengthens our core values which are: Respect, Excellence, Leadership, Loyalty, Integrity, and Selfless Service.


Who we are

As one of the fastest-growing academic health centers in the nation, Texas A&M Health encompasses five colleges and numerous centers and institutes working together to improve health through transformative education, innovative research and team-based health care delivery.


What we want

The Program Coordinator, Rural Medicine Outreach supports the day-to-day administrative and operational functions of the Texas A&M University Naresh K. Vashisht College of Medicine Rural Medicine Outreach Team. Working under the direction of the Director of Rural Medicine Outreach, this position coordinates program operations, student clinical rotation logistics, administrative processes, scheduling, communications, records, and special projects that support the Rural Medicine Program. The position serves as a primary administrative resource for students, faculty, staff, healthcare partners, and community stakeholders, helping ensure timely communication, accurate program records, effective coordination, and consistent follow-through across Rural Medicine activities. Some statewide travel may be required.


What you need to know

Salary: Compensation will be commensurate to the selected hire’s experience.

Schedule: Occasional evening and weekend work may be required to support student clinical rotations, outreach events, health fairs, educational programs, conferences, and community engagement activities.

Travel: Persons in this position should have the ability to travel independently throughout Texas, including frequent overnight travel, by driving and/or flying to support student clinical rotations, partner visits, meetings, conferences, and outreach activities.

Cover Letter/Resume: A cover letter and resume are strongly recommended and will help in our review. You may upload them on the application under the CV/Resume section.


Please note: This position is grant funded; future employment may be contingent upon future funding.

Qualifications

Required Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in an applicable field or an equivalent combination of education and experience
  • Two (2) years of related experience in program coordination, higher education, healthcare, administrative support, event coordination, customer service, student services, or a related field

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's degree or Master of Public Health (MPH) from an accredited college or university
  • Experience working in a healthcare setting, higher education, hospitals, nonprofit organizations, or community-based programs
  • Experience coordinating student programs, outreach initiatives, events, or special projects
  • Valid Texas Class "C" Driver's License or the ability to obtain one within 30 days of employment

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Excellent verbal, written, interpersonal, and customer service skills
  • Ability to communicate effectively and professionally with students, faculty, physicians, healthcare professionals, community leaders, and external partners
  • Strong organizational and project coordination skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and adapt to changing needs
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with colleagues, students, faculty, healthcare professionals, community partners, and external organizations
  • Knowledge of program coordination, event planning, administrative processes, and records management
  • Ability to analyze information, solve problems, and exercise sound judgment in a fast-paced environment
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and Teams) and the ability to learn new software applications
  • Ability to prepare reports, presentations, correspondence, and other professional business documents
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively as part of a team
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information with professionalism and discretion
  • Ability to travel throughout Texas and represent the Rural Medicine Program and the Naresh K. Vashisht College of Medicine in a professional manner
  • Ability to multitask, prioritize competing responsibilities, and maintain attention to detail

Responsibilities

Program Planning, Student Rotation Operations & Implementation:

  • Coordinate the daily operations of rural student rotations and outreach initiatives within the Rural Medicine Program
  • Coordinate student clinical rotations throughout Texas by arranging schedules, travel, housing, onboarding requirements, documentation, and other program logistics
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for students before, during, and after rural clinical rotations
  • Facilitate communication among students, faculty, physicians, hospitals, clinics, and community partners to support successful clinical rotations and program activities
  • Monitor student placements, maintain rotation schedules, and ensure program requirements and deadlines are completed in a timely manner
  • Conduct statewide travel as required
  • Meet with physicians, hospital and clinic leadership, school district representatives, and community stakeholders
  • Support partnership development and community engagement efforts
  • Plan, implement, and assist in evaluating initiatives that support the goals and objectives of the Rural Medicine Program

Program Administration, Records Management & Reporting:

  • Administer daily operational functions that support rural medicine outreach and student clinical rotations
  • Maintain program records, databases, affiliation agreements, calendars, compliance documentation, travel records, housing information, and other program files to support efficient program operations
  • Coordinate travel arrangements and make travel reservations for students and staff, including lodging, transportation, airfare, rental vehicles, and other travel-related logistics
  • Process payments, travel reimbursements, student and staff reimbursements, purchasing requests, invoices, and other administrative and financial transactions in accordance with university procedures
  • Coordinate meetings, workshops, conferences, outreach events, and special projects by scheduling activities, arranging logistics, preparing materials, and facilitating follow-up communications
  • Prepare reports, presentations, correspondence, meeting materials, and other program documentation
  • Compile program statistics, participation data, and outcome measures to support reporting, grant activities, program evaluation, and continuous improvement
  • Track program activities, deadlines, expenses, and administrative processes while maintaining systems that improve operational efficiency, organization, and reporting accuracy

Partnership Development & Community Engagement:

  • Develop and maintain collaborative relationships with hospitals, clinics, physicians, school districts, community organizations, local governments, and other stakeholders to strengthen rural medical education and healthcare workforce development across Texas
  • Coordinate partner visits, stakeholder meetings, community engagement activities, and educational outreach initiatives that support student clinical rotations and promote healthcare careers in rural and underserved communities
  • Plan, coordinate, and support school visits, presentations, career exploration events, workshops, summer camps, and other educational outreach programs in collaboration with school districts, university departments, healthcare organizations, and community partners
  • Represent the Rural Medicine Program and the Naresh K. Vashisht College of Medicine at meetings, conferences, recruitment events, health fairs, partner visits, and community outreach activities throughout Texas
  • Coordinate community immersion experiences that connect medical students with local healthcare professionals, educators, community leaders, and community organizations while enhancing students' understanding of rural healthcare
  • Execute special projects that advance the goals and strategic initiatives of the Rural Medicine Program
  • Collaborate with Business Affairs, Student Affairs, Marketing and Communications, faculty, and other university departments to support program initiatives and achieve departmental objectives

Why Texas A&M University?

We are a prestigious university with strong traditions, Core Values, and a community of caring and collaboration. Amenities associated with a major university, such as sporting and cultural events, state-of-the-art recreation facilities, the Bush Library and Museum, and much more await you. Experience all that a big city has to offer but with a reasonable cost-of-living and no long commutes.

  • Medical, prescription drug, dental, vision, life and AD&D, flexible spending accounts, and long-term disability insurance with Texas A&M contributing to employee health and basic life premiums
  • 12-15 days of annual paid holidays
  • Up to eight hours of paid sick leave and at least eight hours of paid vacation each month
  • Automatic enrollment in the Teacher Retirement System of Texas
  • Health and Wellness: Free exercise programs and release time
  • Professional Development: All employees have access to free LinkedIn Learning training, webinars, and limited financial support to attend conferences, workshops, and more
  • Educational release time and tuition assistance for completing a degree while a Texas A&M employee
  • Living Well, a program at Texas A&M that has been built by employees, for employees

description:
I MENY elsker vi mat! For oss er god mat en lidenskap, og noe av det viktigste som finnes. Hos oss er alle MATarbeidere, uansett om du jobber i ferskvaredisken, kolonialen, i kassen eller på kontoret. Å være en MATarbeider i MENY betyr at du alltid gjør ditt beste for å veilede og inspirere kundene våre til matglede. Sammen skal vi hjelpe flere å spise bedre, og leve bedre.

Stillingsomfang: 100%
Arbeidstid: dag, kveld og annenhver helg
Oppstart: 01.11.26 - eller etter avtale
Søknadsfrist: snarest - eller etter avtale

For å søke på stillingen må du ha fylt 18 år. Du må også kunne kommunisere godt med kunder og kolleger på norsk.

Hvem er du og hva skal du gjøre?
MATarbeiderne i kassen er butikkens fremste ambassadører, og kanskje er du den eneste butikkansatte kunden har kontakt med i løpet av handleturen. Som kasserer vil din hovedoppgave være å slå inn varer, ta i mot betaling og få kunden til å føle seg velkommen. Du vil også fungere som kassevert i de selvbetjente kassene, hente kurver, rydde, fylle varer og hjelpe kunder.

Periodevis vil det være mange kunder og mye som skal gjøres, derfor må du trives med et hektisk tempo og å jobbe med mennesker. Å gi god kunderservice må være en selvfølge for deg, og du smiler til de rundt deg selv om det er mye å gjøre. Vi ønsker oss en ny kasserer med godt humør, sporty innstilling og en som ser løsninger der andre blir frustrerte.

Hvordan er det å jobbe i MENY?
Hos oss vil du blant annet lære å ta ansvar, mestre stress, håndtere mennesker og ikke minst butikkdrift. Vi har en interaktiv kursplattform, ulike klasseromskurs som gir deg faglig påfyll og et traineeprogram med fokus på å gå fra ansatt til å bli leder, for å nevne noe. Satser du på MENY, satser MENY på deg!

Når du starter, skal vi ta deg godt imot og gi deg den opplæringen du trenger. Alle ansatte i MENY får selvfølgelig uniform, lønn etter tariff og subsidiert kantine. I tillegg har vi sosiale sammenkomster i ny og ne, rabatt på treningssenter og arbeidstider som ofte passer godt i kombinasjon med studier. Når det gjelder trivsel på jobb, vil vi trekke frem samholdet. Som en av våre matarbeidere blir du en del av et team som jobber mot felles mål, for din innsats vil påvirke butikken, kundene og kollegene dine. Vi verdsetter gjensidig omtanke og støtte, og det er rom for feil så lenge du lærer og utvikler deg – for er du trygg er du god. Vår visjon er at vår lidenskap endrer folks matvaner, og det håper vi du vil bidra til.

Å søke jobb i MENY skal være enkelt
Du trenger ikke laste opp søknadsbrev. For at vi skal bli litt bedre kjent med deg, svarer du på spørsmålene om deg og din erfaring. Har du mye på hjertet må du gjerne skrive utfyllende, vi gleder oss til å lese! Og fordi vi synes det er spennende å se hvor du har vært tidligere, må du laste opp CV.

Vi gjør oppmerksom på at alle søknader må sendes inn via søknadsskjema tilknyttet annonsen, vi vil ikke ta imot søknader på papir i butikken eller på e-post. Søknader behandles fortløpende.

title: Senior Prospect Analyst, Philanthropic Due Diligence
description:
As George Washington University expands its global fundraising and engagement efforts, the need for consistent and reliable due diligence research continues to grow. Advancement teams are working with an increasingly diverse pool of donors, including individuals, corporations, foundations, and international stakeholders, requiring thoughtful evaluation of potential reputational, ethical, and compliance considerations.

The Senior Prospect Analyst, Philanthropic Due Diligence, supports this effort by conducting due diligence research and contributing to review processes. This role helps ensure that decisions related to donor engagement are informed by accurate, well-documented research and aligned with university policies and values.

Due diligence activities are currently managed within the Research and Relationship Management team alongside other prospect research and relationship management functions. This role enhances the team’s capacity by providing dedicated analytical support, improving consistency in reporting, and helping manage increasing research volume.

**Key Responsibilities**

• Conduct due diligence research on individuals, corporations, foundations, and international entities, including review of reputational, legal, financial, and compliance-related considerations such as adverse media, sanctions, and politically exposed persons.

• Prepare clear, structured, and concise due diligence reports that summarize findings and highlight potential risks for internal stakeholders and for the university as a whole.

• Support established due diligence workflows, including intake, documentation, and tracking of research requests and outcomes.

• Assist in maintaining and applying due diligence guidelines, templates, and documentation standards to ensure consistency and quality.

• Collaborate with prospect research, relationship management, and advancement staff to fulfill research requests and provide background information to support donor strategy.

• Respond to inquiries from internal stakeholders by providing research findings and clarification within defined processes and guidelines.

• Oversee the proposal clearance/clearance to solicit process by managing the process and contributing due diligence research and ensuring relevant information is documented for review.

• Utilize internal and external research tools (e.g., LexisNexis, Factiva, Dow Jones, public records) to gather and verify information.

• Assist in monitoring emerging risks and flagging findings for escalation to senior team members as appropriate.

• Contribute to process improvements and efficiencies within due diligence research workflows.

Performs other related duties as assigned. The omission of specific duties does not preclude the supervisor from assigning duties that are logically related to the position.

title: Build Reliability Engineer II
description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

The Build Reliability Engineer II partners closely with the design and manufacturing teams to right-size processes and controls to enable scaling the production of spacecraft hardware. Build Reliability Engineers ensure production processes yield verified, reliable hardware at rate. You will flex beyond Build Reliability to support Quality, Flight Reliability, and Mission Assurance. The ideal candidate is a responsible, collaborative, process-oriented engineer with hands-on hardware design/test/manufacturing/troubleshooting experience.

Responsibilities

  • Partner with design engineering and manufacturing teams to create test, manufacturability, and inspection plans for all vehicle hardware.
  • Contain suspect or known non-conforming product, providing guidance to quality inspectors, technicians, shop supervisors, and engineers.
  • Lead failure investigations in production, test, and operation; identifying and mitigating immediate and underlying root causes to reduce risk and improve the reliability of designs and processes.
  • Provide critical peer review of hardware during design reviews and acceptance and qualification test campaigns.
  • Perform failure modes and effects analyses, build requirements compliance matrix tools, and ensure adequate test coverage, change management, and manufacturability of flight hardware.
  • Own vehicle level deliverables for regulatory bodies including requirements compliance, functional or flight hazard analyses, and verification evidence.
  • Support Mission Assurance's vehicle level risk management and identification/tracking/execution of mitigations.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in aerospace, computer science, electrical, manufacturing, mechanical, or material sciences engineering.
  • 3+ years professional experience in aerospace, design, quality, or related engineering role.
  • Hands-on hardware test, qualification, troubleshooting, or failure analysis experience.
  • Commitment to lean quality principles without compromising safety or reliability.
  • Demonstrated application of process controls in high volume manufacturing, test, and quality environments.
  • Experience generating, processing, and/or analyzing data for production insight.
  • Strong interpersonal and collaborative skills, with a drive to innovate and improve reliability in cutting-edge technology.

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • Full project lifecycle ownership experience (cradle-to-grave).
  • Proficiency with quality tools such as measurement systems analysis, design of experiments, statistical process control, root cause analysis and corrective action, advanced product quality planning (APQP), metrology, process failure mode and effects analysis (PFMEA), control plans, and various problem-solving approaches.
  • Hands-on knowledge of CNC machining, additive manufacturing, casting, welding, fastening, or other special manufacturing processes.

Pay Range

  • Salary range: Engineer II: $119,543 - $152,749/ per year.
  • This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA.
  • Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance.
  • You will be eligible for incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards.

ITAR Requirements

Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.

“US person” means: U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) (i.e., individual admitted to the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum).

Vi har en interaktiv kursplattform, ulike klasseromskurs som gir deg faglig påfyll og et traineeprogram med fokus på å gå fra ansatt til å bli leder, for å nevne noe. Satser du på MENY, satser MENY på deg!

MENY Bjørvika ligger i et veldig kult område og som stadig vokser. Litt uvanlig for vår butikk er at vi har sushi take-away og Wolt. Det er det ikke mange butikker som har.


Vi er en ungdommelig gjeng og bryr oss om hverandre. Vi liker å bli godt kjent, og snakker derfor mye med hverandre gjennom arbeidsdagen. Vi tror at når man er bedre kjent, så har man det mer gøy på jobb, det skaper god energi.


Vi har dessuten takhøyde, vi liker at du kommer med gode ideer og innspill. Er du typen som liker å komme med initiativ vil du passe rett inn. Med nye tanker og ideer er det ikke bare butikken som utvikler seg, men også deg som medarbeider. Velkommen!


Å søke jobb i MENY skal være enkelt
Du trenger ikke laste opp søknadsbrev. For at vi skal bli litt bedre kjent med deg, svarer du på spørsmålene om deg og din erfaring. Har du mye på hjertet må du gjerne skrive utfyllende, vi gleder oss til å lese! Og fordi vi synes det er spennende å se hvor du har vært tidligere, må du laste opp CV.


Vi gjør oppmerksom på at alle søknader må sendes inn via søknadsskjema tilknyttet annonsen, dette er av hensyn til ditt personvern, samt at vi ønsker å være sikre på at vi klarer å følge opp alle kandidater på en god måte. Vi kan derfor ikke ta imot søknader på papir i butikken eller via e-post. Søknader behandles fortløpende.

Job Description

Job no: 502915
Work type: Full Time Permanent

Data Systems Specialist

  • Join a collaborative team proud of its role in keeping our skies safe
  • Combine aviation experience with data systems shaping airspace operations

Summary

Use your aviation experience to optimise and manage operational systems within the National Airways System. Drive safety, performance, and innovation.

The Organisation

Airservices Australia is a government-owned organisation responsible for the safe, secure and efficient management of 11 per cent of the world’s airspace and the provision of Aviation Rescue Fire Fighting Services at Australia’s busiest airports.

With operations across Australia, our people play a critical role in ensuring Australia’s aviation network remains among the safest in the world. We value expertise, collaboration and a strong safety culture, and offer meaningful careers in a dynamic and evolving industry.

The Role & The Team

As a Data Systems Specialist within the Technology Enablement group, you will be responsible for managing the integrity, configuration and adaptation of operational airways systems that underpin the National Airways System (NAS).

In this role, you will work closely with operational stakeholders, technical specialists and project teams to develop, maintain and implement system data that directly impacts aviation safety, operational efficiency and standardisation. You will analyse change requests, prepare and adapt system data, support training and operational systems, and ensure all changes comply with mandated procedures and regulatory standards.

The team is highly technical, collaborative and safety-focused, and is proud of the role it plays in delivering reliable, trusted systems that support air traffic services nationally.

Please see the link below to view the full Position Description.

You are analytical, methodical and comfortable working in a safety-critical operational environment. You take pride in accuracy and quality, enjoy solving complex problems and can adapt effectively to changing priorities.

The successful applicant will have:

  • Demonstrated experience working with operational or technical systems in an Air Traffic Control, aviation or similarly regulated environment
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience managing complex data or system configurations
  • Ability to interpret technical requirements and translate them into effective system adaptations
  • Well-developed communication skills to engage with a broad range of operational and technical stakeholders
  • Experience working within structured procedures, safety frameworks and mandated timelines

Qualifications in Information Technology, Engineering, Aviation, or equivalent demonstrated experience are highly regarded.

At Airservices Australia, we embrace diversity of thought, experience and perspective. We actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.

Security Clearance

To be eligible to apply, you must be an Australian Citizen, as this role requires the ability to obtain and maintain an Australian Government security clearance. Security checks will be undertaken as part of the recruitment process.

Vas navdušuje usklajevanje kompleksnih proizvodnih planov, sodelovanje z različnimi deležniki in sprejemanje odločitev, ki vplivajo na uspešno oskrbo pacientov? Kot Taktični planer boste prevzeli ključne procese taktičnega planiranja ter igrali osrednjo vlogo pri usklajevanju povpraševanja, zmogljivosti in razpoložljivosti virov. Odgovorni boste za tedensko planiranje na DFB področju, dolgoročno načrtovanje vhodnih materialov, surovin in potrošnega materiala ter tesno sodelovanje z end-to-end planerji pri usklajevanju potreb trga. Aktivno boste sodelovali v procesu prodajnega in operativnega planiranja (S&OP), spremljali ključne kazalnike uspešnosti oskrbe ter prispevali k optimizaciji procesov in učinkovitemu načrtovanju prihodnjih aktivnosti in projektov. To je odlična priložnost za analitičnega in proaktivnega posameznika, ki želi s svojim delom pomembno vplivati na zanesljivost oskrbne verige in poslovne rezultate.


Job Description

Vaše ključne odgovornosti:

  • Vodenje taktičnega planiranja proizvodnje za obdobje od 5 do 24 mesecev skladno s povpraševanjem.
  • Zagotavljanje ustreznih proizvodnih zmogljivosti, virov in materialov za nemoteno izvedbo proizvodnih planov.
  • Izvajanje tedenskega planiranja na DFB področju ter dolgoročnega planiranja surovin, materialov in potrošnega materiala.
  • Usklajevanje z end-to-end planerji glede usklajevanja potreb trga.
  • Aktivno vodenje in podpora procesu prodajnega in operativnega planiranja (S&OP).
  • Spremljanje, analiza in poročanje o ključnih kazalnikih uspešnosti oskrbe, vključno z NOSCE kazalniki.
  • Upravljanje parametrov planiranja v sistemih SAP in Rapid Response ter zagotavljanje kakovosti podatkov.
  • Sodelovanje pri stalnih izboljšavah procesov, optimizaciji zalog in doseganju ciljev uspešnosti oskrbe.

Vaš doprinos k delovnem mestu:

  • Visokošolska izobrazba tehnične, ekonomske, logistične ali druge ustrezne smeri.
  • Najmanj eno leto izkušenj na področju oskrbne verige, nabave, proizvodnje ali sorodnih funkcij.
  • Aktivno znanje slovenskega in angleškega jezika, tako v pisni kot ustni komunikaciji.
  • Dobro poznavanje orodij Microsoft Office in sposobnost dela s podatki ter analizami.
  • Visoka stopnja natančnosti, doslednosti in odgovornosti pri načrtovanju ter upravljanju prioritet.
  • Sposobnost pravočasnega prepoznavanja tveganj, ustreznega stopnjevanja izzivov in občutek za nujnost pri sprejemanju odločitev.


Zaželene izkušnje:

  • Proaktiven pristop k izboljševanju procesov in iskanju učinkovitih rešitev.
  • Dobro poznavanje digitalnih orodij ter zanimanje za napredne analitične in umetno-inteligenčne rešitve.

Z izbranim kandidatom bomo sklenili delovno razmerje za določen čas enega leta s poskusno dobo 6 mesecev. Prijavo oddajte z življenjepisom v slovenskem in angleškem jeziku.

Nagrajevanje:

V Novartisu smo zavezani k soustvarjanju prihodnosti medicine ter priznavanju in nagrajevanju ljudi, ki to omogočajo.


Pričakovani letni osnovni razpon plače za delovno mesto:

32.060,00 - 59.540,00 EUR


Osnovna plača se določa na podlagi vnaprej opredeljenih in transparentnih kriterijev, kot so relevantne veščine, kompetence in izkušnje, ne glede na spol, ter v skladu z Novartisovo politiko določanja plač. Po zaposlitvi v Novartisu se plača periodično pregleda v skladu z internimi akti in postopki.


Plačna enakost je temeljno načelo naše kadrovske politike in odraža našo zavezo k ustvarjanju raznolikega, pravičnega in vključujočega okolja, ki vse zaposlene obravnava dostojanstveno in spoštljivo, kot je opredeljeno v našem Kodeksu etike.


Poleg osnovne letne bruto plače so zaposleni upravičeni tudi do spodaj navedenih ugodnosti:

  • Letni bonus, ki pripada vsakemu zaposlenemu: 12% letne plače.
  • Regres za dopust: Leta 2025 je znašal 2.496 € (neto). Za leto 2026 znaša 2.678,28 € (neto).
  • Nagrada za poslovno uspešnost: Leta 2025 je znašala 2.538,64 € (bruto), skupaj z zimskim regresom.
  • Prostovoljno dodatno pokojninsko zavarovanje: Novartis v Sloveniji zagotavlja prostovoljno dodatno pokojninsko zavarovanje (5,844 % bruto izplačila, letno omejeno na 3.224,18 €).
  • Zavarovanje: Dodatno nezgodno zavarovanje: V času zaposlitve pri Novartisu je zaposleni 24/7 zavarovan za primer smrti ali invalidnosti, ki bi bila posledica nezgode. Zavarovanje – Specialisti: Kolektivno zdravstveno zavarovanje, ki omogoča hitrejši dostop do specialističnih zdravstvenih storitev pri Zavarovalnici Triglav d.d. za vas in vaše družinske člane.
  • Care Connect: Program, ki ponuja zaupno, osebno podporo za vaše duševno zdravje in dobro počutje s pomočjo terapij, svetovanj, orodij in še mnogo več.
  • Ostale ugodnosti v skladu z zakonom in kolektivno pogodbo: Prevoz, prehrana ter ostali dodatki.

Preberite brošuro in izvedite več o našem sistemu nagrajevanja:


Opomba: Ugodnosti se lahko razlikujejo glede na državo ter so skladni z lokalno zakonodajo, vključno z določili kolektivnih pogodb. Celovit pregled vašega paketa prejemkov, vključno z morebitnimi relevantnimi določbami kolektivne pogodbe, ki veljajo za vašo delovno mesto glede na lokacijo zaposlitve in delodajalca Novartis, vam bo posredovan v okviru nadaljnjih korakov zaposlitvenega postopka.


Predani smo raznolikosti in vključenosti: Novartis si prizadeva ustvariti izjemno, vključujoče delovno okolje in oblikovanje raznolikih timov, saj ti predstavljajo naše bolnike in skupnosti, ki jih oskrbujemo.


Zakaj Novartis: Pomagati bolnikom in njihovim družinam zahteva več kot le inovativno znanost. Potrebna je skupnost zavzetih ljudi, kot ste vi. V Novartisu cenimo sodelovanje, podporo in navdihovanje drug drugega za razvoj prebojnih terapij, ki spreminjajo življenja pacientov. Ste pripravljeni ustvariti svetlejšo prihodnost skupaj z nami?

title: Lead Engineer - Power Conversion & Controls
description:
Job Description Summary

Collaborate with a small group of power conversion and controls engineers, plus the wider engineering and product teams across GE and its customers, to design and develop Aviation Power Electronic Conversion products. As a Lead Engineer - Power Conversion & Controls, you will contribute to converters, inverters, and energy storage solutions and systems. Based in Dayton, OH, you will help develop technology and product roadmaps, oversee product bids and proposal activities, and work directly with engineering teams to solve technical issues. You will do this by supervising their work and by conducting analyses yourself. Your work will support the successful development and implementation of Aviation Power Generation and Conversion products for our Electric Power and Propulsion customers.

This role has real technical influence and visibility. You will use your depth in power conversion and controls to shape product direction, guide teams through technical problems, and help leadership see where customer needs and product capabilities differ.

Job Description

In this role you will:


  • Work with customers and internal commercial and engineering component teams to architect electrical power systems for the Aviation/Aerospace industry.
  • Coordinate diverse teams to execute power converter trade studies and analyses.
  • Apply the latest Aviation industry standards in your work, and help develop new standards for emerging technologies.
  • Use model-based analytical tools to develop and optimize electrical power systems, in conjunction with electrical power component engineers.
  • Work with suppliers of both internally and externally sourced electrical power components.
  • Review customer requirements for leadership and highlight differences and gaps between those requirements and product capabilities.
  • Work with the internal and external design team to test overall electrical power systems and troubleshoot issues.
  • Supervise engineering team work and conduct your own analyses to solve technical issues.

SUMMARY:

The School of Music at East Texas A&M University invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant/Associate Professor in Music (Director of Choral Activities). The successful candidate will provide artistic, academic, and programmatic leadership for the University's choral program while contributing to teaching, Research, Scholarship, and Creative Activities (RSCA), recruitment, outreach, and service. The position includes a reduced teaching load to accommodate administrative duties, in consultation annually with the Director of the School of Music.

The School of Music serves approximately 240 music majors across instrumental, vocal, and keyboard areas and is fully accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). It offers baccalaureate and master's degrees in music education and performance and a Bachelor of Arts in Music. The School is housed in a $30 million music building completed in 2010 containing state-of-the-art recital and concert halls, studios, rehearsal halls, classrooms, and teaching areas.

The University Chorale has an established record of significant artistic and educational achievement, including performances at Carnegie Hall, the International Music Festival of Campina Grande in Brazil, venues in France and Austria, and the 2019 Texas Music Educators Association Convention.

The Director will lead the University Chorale and Chamber Singers; teach undergraduate and graduate courses in choral conducting, choral literature, and related areas; mentor students; and contribute to the continued growth, visibility, and reputation of the choral program through high-quality performance, programming, recruitment, outreach, and professional engagement.

The position includes an administrative release; duties will be determined based on qualifications, administrative experience, demonstrated leadership skills, and School of Music needs.


DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

Choral Program Leadership and Artistic Direction

  • Provide artistic, educational, and programmatic leadership for the University's choral program.
  • Direct the University Chorale and Chamber Singers and oversee their artistic development, rehearsal, performance, and long-term growth.
  • Establish high standards for ensemble musicianship, vocal technique, diction, interpretation, and performance.
  • Develop an artistic vision and select repertoire representing a breadth of historical periods, styles, composers, languages, and world/cultural contexts.
  • Plan concert programming and pursue appropriate performance, touring, festival, conference, and collaborative opportunities.
  • Participate in strategic planning and program development for the continued growth of choral activities.

Teaching and Student Development

  • Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in choral conducting, choral literature, and related areas as assigned.
  • Provide instruction in conducting technique, score study, rehearsal methodology, choral pedagogy, repertoire, and ensemble leadership.
  • Mentor and advise students pursuing careers in music education, conducting, performance, and related fields.
  • Contribute to curriculum development, assessment, and program review within the choral area and School of Music.

Music Education and Professional Preparation

  • Work with music education faculty to prepare students for careers as music educators and choral professionals.
  • Supervise and mentor student teachers and maintain relationships with cooperating teachers and school administrators.
  • Provide students with opportunities to develop professional skills in choral teaching and conducting.

Recruitment, Retention, and Outreach

  • Provide leadership for recruitment and retention of undergraduate and graduate students in choral music, music education, performance, conducting, and related areas.
  • Develop and implement effective recruitment initiatives and participate in auditions, clinics, workshops, festivals, prospective-student events, and other enrollment activities.
  • Develop relationships with secondary-school choral directors, music educators, community organizations, and other prospective-student constituencies throughout Texas and the region.
  • Represent East Texas A&M University and the School of Music at appropriate professional events and develop partnerships that strengthen the University's connections with schools, communities, and the broader choral profession.

Collaboration and School of Music Leadership

  • Collaborate with faculty and administrators across the School of Music to support student success and program development.
  • Maintain knowledge of vocal technique, vocal health, diction, repertoire, and performance preparation sufficient to address these areas within the choral program and coordinate with vocal faculty as appropriate.
  • Contribute to a collegial, collaborative, and student-centered School of Music environment.

Research, Scholarship, and Creative Activities

  • Pursue creative activity through conducting, performances, recordings, guest conducting, clinics, workshops, master classes, and related professional activities.
  • Engage in scholarly activity appropriate to the candidate's expertise, including research, publication, presentation, or other professional scholarship.
  • Maintain appropriate professional engagement in state, regional, national, and/or international organizations.

Service

  • Participate in service to the School of Music, college, University, profession, and community consistent with the expectations of a tenure-track faculty appointment.
  • Contribute to accreditation, assessment, strategic planning, and other institutional activities as appropriate.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by the Director of the School of Music.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

· Education: Doctorate in Music Education, Choral Conducting, Conducting, or a closely related field from an accredited institution; equivalent university experience and demonstrated achievement may be considered in lieu of the doctorate

· Experience / Knowledge / Skills:

    • Demonstrated professional experience in choral conducting and ensemble leadership.
    • Demonstrated knowledge of choral repertoire, conducting techniques, rehearsal methodology, choral pedagogy, and vocal principles relevant to choral instruction.

· Ability to:

    • Demonstrated ability to conduct, rehearse, and develop choral ensembles.
    • Demonstrated ability to teach and mentor students in a collegiate environment.
    • Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with faculty, staff, students, and professional colleagues.

· Licensing/Professional Certifications: N/A

· Physical Requirements: N/A

· Other Requirements: N/A

PREFERRED EDUCATION / SKILLS/ EXPERIENCE:

  • Significant collegiate teaching and/or choral conducting experience and a record of successful collegiate ensemble leadership.
  • Experience teaching choral conducting and choral literature at the undergraduate and/or graduate level.
  • Demonstrated success in student recruitment, enrollment growth, or development and implementation of effective recruitment initiatives.
  • Experience supervising student teachers and developing partnerships with secondary schools, community organizations, and professional music organizations.
  • Demonstrated record of creative activity and/or scholarship in choral conducting, music education, vocal pedagogy, or a related field.
  • Experience presenting clinics, workshops, lectures, master classes, or conducting sessions.
  • Professional leadership through state, regional, national, and/or international choral or music education organizations.
  • Demonstrated administrative experience involving faculty coordination, curriculum planning, recruitment, assessment, scheduling, program development, or related academic responsibilities.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead collaboratively, communicate effectively, manage competing priorities, and support faculty and student success.
  • Familiarity with contemporary choral pedagogy, vocal health, repertoire encompassing a breadth of historical periods and world/cultural contexts, and evidence-informed music education.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of the University Interscholastic League (UIL) processes, expectations, and procedures governing Texas public school music programs, including concert and sight-reading evaluation, solo and ensemble contests, eligibility requirements, and related compliance responsibilities.
  • Experience preparing students or preservice music educators for successful participation in UIL activities

SUPERVISION OF OTHERS:

NA

description:
WHAT YOU'LL DO

Avenues' distinctive academic program makes our graduates uniquely compelling applicants for the most selective postsecondary pursuits. Deans provide individualized support and expertise, helping identify the best fit for students based on their passions and aspirations. A Dean is a leader (also mentor, cheerleader, confidant, and occasional tough-love-giver) who supports students' wellbeing, partners deeply with their families and supports their journey to what's next. Above all, deans build powerful, lasting relationships with students that extend for years during, and then beyond, their time at Avenues.

Foster students' well-being, through powerful relationships and mentoring

  • Advise and guide 100 students and their families across grades 09-12. Your students will feel known, mentored and supported; their families will rave about you.

  • Ensure students and families feel well-informed and prepared for the college process

Join a dynamic, collaborative team

  • Enthusiastically contribute to a dean team dedicated to all Avenues students' wellbeing

  • You love and respect teenagers. You feel deeply passionate about supporting them to learn, grow, and thrive as people
  • You believe that going to college should be about finding a right match for each student

  • You navigate difficult conversations with grace and empathy
  • You effectively handle multiple priorities in a fast-moving environment

title: Retail Leadership Graduate Program VIC
description:
Retail Leadership Graduate Program VIC

Position Description: Retail Leadership Graduate

Location: AUS & NZ wide

Start: Feb 2027

The program with Reece will build your skills and abilities to begin a career in retail management.

About the opportunity: The program is designed to accelerate the development of those who are passionate about retail management and leadership, business development and creating customers for life. If you'd like to acquire the skills to run a retail branch as if it was your own - this role is for you.

Throughout the 18-month program, you will enjoy:

  • Permanent employment from day 1 with access to unlimited career opportunities in an organisation that promotes and develops our talent from within
  • A comprehensive, blended learning experience to expedite your development including an initial 5-day induction followed by immersive group learning experiences, as well as digital learning tools, on-the-job training, coaching and mentoring support
  • An end-to-end structured development journey covering all aspects of running your own branch, equipping you to succeed as an Assistant Branch Manager once you've completed the program
  • Rotations around select specialty business units
  • Providing advice on products and services in areas as diverse as plumbing, the provision of sustainable clean water and energy efficiency, heating, ventilation, refrigeration, air-conditioning and climate control, sanitation, bathroom, kitchen, irrigation, pools, civil, design and building products.

About You: At Reece, attitude is key. We aim to improve the lives of our customers and our people by striving for greatness every day. We don't expect you to have industry experience - although retail or customer service experience is advantageous. We'd like to hear from you if you have the following:

  • A growth mindset - you love learning and embrace opportunities to grow and develop, continually improving your skills and acquiring new knowledge
  • Strong written and oral communication skills
  • Demonstrated ability to utilise emotional intelligence to establish and build strong relationships
  • The ability to prioritise many competing tasks and organise work so that it is completed efficiently while always keeping the customer first
  • Proven ability to identify and solve problems, acting decisively and show good judgement

About Reece: Reece is an Australian icon - we've been around for 100 years. We're a big business that works hard to retain the little things that made us great when we were small. We live by our values - we also hire by them and promote by them. We take our work seriously but not ourselves.

Much more than plumbing.

You might know us as Australia's largest supplier of plumbing and bathroom products but that's just the start. We're a major public company with over 9,000 people, 900 branches globally, 10 business lines across Australia and New Zealand.

We are heavily focused on logistics, technology and marketing to drive the business forward, we even have a creative agency, innovation centre, and insight hub. This broad skill base helps us solve customer problems in unique ways. We're growing both nationally and internationally and that's where you come in.

Our Perks: In return, you'll be fairly compensated, provided a uniform allowance, and have access to fuel, gym and other awesome product discounts. Plus, you'll have the opportunity to reach your potential and foster a long-lasting career

If you're excited by the idea of working with great people in a thriving business, then Reece may be for you.

title: Principal Systems Engineer
description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

Rocket Lab’s Space Systems division builds complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space including solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, and radios.

The Space Systems division has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. We have built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help get to space — our Space Systems division is empowering the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

PRINCIPAL SYSTEMS ENGINEER

Rocket Lab Optical Systems solves mission-critical space domain and Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance challenges for Department of Defense and Intelligence Community customers. Our vision is to revolutionize the space-based payload market with innovative and novel designs for space, terrestrial, and airborne environments. Building on more than 20 years of electro-optical and infrared systems innovation from Geost, Rocket Lab Optical Systems delivers solutions to the warfighter for responsive, scalable sensing solutions across all orbital domains.

As a Principal Systems Engineer for Rocket Lab Optical Systems in Tucson, AZ, you will be involved throughout the entire lifecycle of advanced space payloads in support of Tranche 3 of the U.S. Space Development Agency's Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

  • Support the development of system architecture for space-based optical instruments, subsystems, and payloads on airborne and space platforms, with emphasis on electrical architecture and controls integration
  • Define, decompose, and manage system requirements with focus on electrical behavior, control functions, subsystem interactions, and overall system performance
  • Develop and maintain technical documentation including architecture descriptions, interface control documents, electrical interface definitions, concepts of operations, state and mode descriptions, test plans, and verification artifacts
  • Support development of electrical and functional architectures, including command and telemetry flow, power distribution, control logic, signal paths, timing, synchronization, and subsystem interaction
  • Collaborate with hardware, software, firmware, and test teams to ensure the electrical architecture and controls implementation align with system requirements and mission intent
  • Support the development, integration, and testing of space payloads to be integrated on spacecraft platforms
  • Support hardware and software development teams with system-level test planning, debugging, integration, and execution of verification procedures; analyze data and recommend design refinements
  • Participate in hardware and software verification and validation activities related to system behavior, electrical performance, controls implementation, and interface compliance
  • Support architecture trades involving sensors, motor control, embedded electronics, power systems, command and data handling, and subsystem interfaces
  • Participate in technical interchange meetings and project discussions with internal teams, customers, and external partners as needed
  • Identify, assess, and help mitigate technical risks related to electrical architecture, controls implementation, and subsystem integration
  • Support travel or off-site work as needed
  • Perform other duties as assigned

QUALIFICATIONS YOU’LL BRING AS PRINCIPAL SYSTEMS ENGINEER:

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical, systems, or aerospace engineering; or other technical discipline
  • 12+ years of engineering experience, including 3+ years supporting development programs and 2+ years in technical leadership, CAM, IPTL, or equivalent role
  • Demonstrated systems engineering experience with emphasis on electrical architecture, subsystem integration, and controls focused development
  • Strong electrical engineering background supporting complex aerospace, payload, avionics, or instrument systems
  • Experience developing system requirements, interface definitions, and verification approaches for complex systems
  • Strong background in electrical interfaces, control functions, avionics integration, or subsystem architecture
  • Experience with requirements management and modeling tools such as JAMA, DOORS, Cameo, or similar tools
  • Experience working across hardware, software, and firmware development throughout the lifecycle
  • Familiarity with command and telemetry interfaces, power architectures, signal interfaces, timing, synchronization, and control logic
  • Experience supporting integration and test, including troubleshooting electrical or controls-related issues at the subsystem or system level
  • Strong ability to read, interpret, and develop electrical, interface, and system technical documentation
  • Familiarity with aerospace development standards, environmental testing, and mission assurance practices

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

  • Current SSBI clearance
  • EO/IR payload integration experience
  • Experience with spacecraft bus interfaces, payload electrical integration, avionics architecture, or embedded electronics
  • Experience with pointing, stabilization, gimbals, motion control, focus/control electronics, or other closed-loop control applications
  • Experience defining or troubleshooting electrical architectures for sensors, actuators, motors, power systems, or embedded controllers
  • Hands-on expertise leading troubleshooting and resolution of system-level electrical or controls-related issues
  • Demonstrated experience working with minimal supervision in complex projects
  • Experience in astronomy, physics, or remote sensing
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to collaborate with multidisciplinary teams and explain complex implementation processes to other organization members
  • Strong communication, task management, and cross-functional coordination skills

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Important information:

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. We’re a technology company with operations in Metro Detroit and Los Angeles, supplying aluminum plate, bar, and rounds to aerospace and defense manufacturers. We use software and automation to supply metal to American factories faster than the industry thought possible.

The role. We’re hiring Associate Supply Chain Engineers to improve how material is bought, positioned, and moved through Nox Metals. You will use data and direct operational work to help the right aluminum reach the right facility at the right time, without hiding problems behind excess inventory.

You will work across purchasing, suppliers, inventory, production, sales, and logistics. This is a strong early-career role for someone who likes analytical problems but wants to see the physical result of their decisions.

You will:

  • Translate demand and inventory data into practical purchasing and transfer recommendations

  • Place and track purchase orders and resolve supplier exceptions

  • Monitor lead times, availability, service levels, and material exposure

  • Analyze shortages, excess, expedite costs, and recurring planning errors

  • Coordinate inbound freight and interfacility material movements

  • Maintain accurate supplier, item, and purchasing data

  • Work with sales and operations to understand priorities and changing demand

  • Build reports and simple tools that improve daily decisions

  • Visit the floor to reconcile system data with physical reality

  • Own improvement projects with measurable cost, availability, or speed outcomes

You are:

  • Analytical, organized, and willing to chase details to the source

  • Comfortable with spreadsheets, data, and quantitative tradeoffs

  • A clear communicator with suppliers and internal teams

  • Curious about manufacturing, inventory, logistics, and physical constraints

  • Calm when a plan changes and disciplined about communicating the impact

  • Willing to do routine transactional work while improving the system around it

  • Accountable for results rather than just recommendations

Nice to have:

  • Degree or experience in supply chain, industrial engineering, operations, analytics, or a related field

  • Experience in purchasing, planning, logistics, manufacturing, or distribution

  • Familiarity with ERP, inventory, or business-intelligence tools

  • Experience with SQL, Python, optimization, or statistical analysis

  • Comfort using AI tools to research, analyze, and automate responsibly

Benefits:

  • Equity in Nox Metals

  • Company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance

This role is full time and in person in either Los Angeles or Detroit.

Nox Metals is an equal opportunity employer. We hire based on skill, attitude, and fit for the work, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, height, weight, marital status, or any other protected status under federal, state, or local law.

General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc. (GA-ASI), an affiliate of General Atomics, is a world leader in proven, reliable remotely piloted aircraft and tactical reconnaissance radars, as well as advanced high-resolution surveillance systems.

Under minimal supervision and working in a loud environment with a variety of epoxy agents, this position builds up, fabricates, cures and assembles various types of composite materials where required information is readily available, methods and sequences have been pre-determined and tooling is provided. title: Scientist I – Analytical Operations
description:
Work Schedule

Standard (Mon-Fri)

Environmental Conditions

Adherence to all Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) Safety Standards, Laboratory Setting, Some degree of PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) required (safety glasses, gowning, gloves, lab coat, ear plugs etc.)

Job Description

Summary:

Provide analytical support in the Laboratory Operations Department by following standard practices. Perform analytical testing as assigned for on prototype, CTM (Clinical Trial Material) and Commercial batches supporting development and/or manufacturing operations. Make detailed observations and review, document, and communicate test results.

Essential Functions:

  • Document all experimental data in accordance with Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original and Accurate (ALCOA).
  • Carry out independently HPLC, dissolution and physical testing analysis testing following established procedures Analytical Methods & Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
  • Work Proficiency with Empower, NuGenesis, MS Word & Excel Software.
  • Perform basic troubleshooting to overcome system suitability failures.
  • Recognize and report unexpected or Out Of Specification (OOS) results immediately to the Supervisor and conducts laboratory investigations under direction.
  • Maintain a safe working environment and report potential hazards.
  • Perform alternating or rotating shift work (as required)

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

Education:

B.Sc. in chemistry.

Experience:

Experience with common laboratory equipment and operations.

Equivalency:

Equivalent combinations of education, training, and relevant work experience may be considered.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

Understanding of basic chemistry. Understanding of chromatographic separations. Knowledge of qualitative and quantitative chemical or microbiological analysis. Awareness of quality and regulatory requirements in the pharmaceutical industry. Good problem-solving skills and logical approach to solving scientific problems. Demonstrable interpersonal and communication skills (both oral and written). Ability to read and interpret technical procedures and governmental regulations. Ability to apply mathematical operations to such tasks as determination of test reliability, analysis of variance, and correlation techniques. Works well independently and in a team environment. Demonstrated computer proficiency with Microsoft Office programs. Proficiency in the English Language.

Standards and Expectations:

Follow all Environmental Health & Safety Policies and Procedures. Work collaboratively with fellow team members, modelling positive team principles and partnering to meet project and departmental objectives. Carry out all duties within strict compliance to Patheon quality systems Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP). Maintain workspace in a clean and orderly fashion. Actively engage in and adhere to departmental systems to maintain a smooth and efficient workflow (visual management, scheduling systems, etc.). Be client and patient conscious at all times. Understand Key Performance Indicators and strive to improve the performance of the team by identifying areas for system improvements and engage in problem solving. Model positive thinking and is open to change, motivating the team to adapt to shifts in priorities and new ways of working. Proactively identify areas for improvement in the execution of procedures. Communicate risks to timelines in a proactive manner. Consistently strives to improve skills and knowledge in related field.

Physical Requirements:

Position requires ordinary ambulatory skills and physical coordination sufficient to move about lab/office locations; ability to stand, walk, stoop, kneel, crouch periodically for prolonged periods of time; manipulation (lift, carry, move) of light to medium weights of 10-35 pound pounds; arm, hand and finger dexterity, including ability to grasp and type for prolonged periods of time; visual acuity to use a keyboard, computer monitor, operate equipment, and read materials for prolonged periods of time; ability to sit, reach with hands and arms, talk, and hear for prolonged periods of time. Safety glasses, safety shoes, lab coat, latex or similar gloves, safety apron, organic respirator occasionally.

Compensation

The estimated annualized pay range for this position in Ontario is $51,200.00–$76,850.00.
